title: A punctured active-root tower splitting trivializes a finite normalization after strict localization
statement:
Let $p$ be a positive prime and let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian $\mathbf F_p$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Choose $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in B$, $r\geq0$, with $f=\prod_i t_i$ (empty product $1$) having injective multiplication on $B$. For each positive $m$ prime to $p$, put
$$C_m=B[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^m-t_i)_i,$$
and assume $C_m$ is normal, meaning that every prime localization is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $D$ be a finite $B[1/f]$-algebra etale over $B[1/f]$, and put $D_m=D\otimes_{B[1/f]}C_m[1/f]$ and $E_m=\operatorname{IntCl}_{C_m}(D_m)$, the integral closure of $C_m$ in $D_m$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category, def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-integral-closure].
Fix a geometric point $\bar v$ of $\operatorname{Spec}B$, with image $v$, and let $A=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B,\bar v}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ with its structural map from $B$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Set $I=\{i:t_i(v)=0\}$ and
$$T_m=A[z_i:i\in I]/(z_i^m-t_i)_{i\in I},\qquad Q_m=T_m[1/f].$$
The image of each inactive $t_j$ is a unit in $A$, so $Q_m$ also denotes the localization at $\prod_{i\in I}t_i$. Use transitions $z_{i,m}\mapsto z_{i,m'}^{m'/m}$ for $m\mid m'$ and let $Q_\infty=\varinjlim_{(m,p)=1}Q_m$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Suppose a nonnegative integer $d$ and a $Q_\infty$-algebra isomorphism
$$\theta_\infty:D\otimes_{B[1/f]}Q_\infty\simeq Q_\infty^{d}$$
are given. Then there is a positive $m$ prime to $p$ and a $Q_m$-algebra isomorphism $\theta_m:D\otimes_{B[1/f]}Q_m\simeq Q_m^d$ whose scalar extension to $Q_\infty$ is exactly $\theta_\infty$.
For this $m$, let $S_m=A\otimes_B C_m$, with the $T_m$-algebra map $z_i\mapsto x_i$ for active $i$. Scalar extension of $\theta_m$ gives an $S_m[1/f]$-algebra isomorphism $D_m\otimes_{C_m}S_m\simeq S_m[1/f]^d$. The integral closure of $S_m$ in $S_m[1/f]$ is the structural image of $S_m$, and this splitting restricts to an $S_m$-algebra isomorphism
$$E_m\otimes_B A\simeq S_m^{d}.$$
Consequently the actual normalization $\operatorname{Spec}E_m$ becomes a trivial finite etale cover of $\operatorname{Spec}S_m$ after base change along $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}B$. No regularity of $A$, Galois group, invertible cover degree, or choice of roots of unity is assumed. Empty covers, $d=0$, and $r=0$ are allowed.

proof.text: The small-model affine-chart theorem, applied to the identity chart of Spec B and the prescribed presentation e, gives B -> A ind-etale. Transfer the local-ring structure of the chosen strict-henselization ring to A via full faithfulness of Spec. The small-to-full comparison and the closed-point theorem show that the closed point of Spec A maps to v. Hence a parameter outside the specified active set has image outside the maximal ideal of A and is a unit.
Etaleness gives finite presentation of D. Apply the specified active-root splitting descent theorem to obtain m, theta_m and its required agreement with theta at infinity.

Apply the already proved flat root-tower nonzerodivisor theorem with the identity flat map B -> B, the set of all positive orders, and the identity flat map out of its ring colimit. Its finite-stage conjunct gives regularity of f on C_m, including r=0. Apply the punctured-stage integral-closure theorem with this regularity, the normality hypothesis at m, and B -> A ind-etale.

Apply fixed-stage normalization restriction to theta_m, using the puncture injection and the characterization of integral elements just obtained. It supplies k, its coefficient and root equations, Theta and epsilon with the actual ambient-inclusion equality. Combine these witnesses with theta_m and its colimit equation, and insert the separately obtained integral-closedness conjunct. This is exactly the original conclusion.
